decision.explanation: The evidence from the phase I study of pazopanib and vorinostat in advanced solid tumors supports the claim. Specifically, in the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer, those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations (including TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C) had significantly longer median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) compared to TP53-undetected cases. This indicates that the presence of these specific TP53 mutations is associated with a positive response/sensitivity to the combination therapy of pazopanib and vorinostat in colorectal cancer. The evidence direction is SUPPORTS, the evidence type is PREDICTIVE (as it predicts response based on mutation status), the molecular profile matches the specified variants, the significance is sensitivity/response (improved PFS/OS), the therapies are Pazopanib and Vorinostat in combination, and the variant origin is SOMATIC (as these are hotspot mutations in tumor samples).

citations.quote:
In the phase I study of pazopanib and vorinostat in 36 patients with advanced solid tumors, detection of hotspot TP53 mutation was associated with a higher rate of SD ≥6 months/PR, longer median PFS (months), and longer median OS (months) compared to patients without a hotspot TP53 mutation. 
In colorectal cancer cases, detected TP53 hotspot mutations included TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C.

In the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and sarcoma treated with pazopanib and vorinostat, those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations (n = 6) had a significantly longer median PFS of 6.5 months (95% CI 3.0–9.0; p = 0.023) compared to 2.0 months (95% CI 1.8–2.2; p = 0.023) in TP53-undetected cases (n = 10), and a significantly longer median OS of 19.8 months (95% CI 8.2–31.4; p = 0.021) versus 7.2 months (95% CI 0.6–13.8; p = 0.021), respectively.
